title: Which forms are equal to the given expression?
description: Two given expressions are each compared with four forms, by reading the terms with their signs. Forms with the same terms are equal, and forms that change a term, a product or a sign are not.
teaching_notes: One idea: two expressions are equal when they have the same terms with the same signs, and a change in one number must be cancelled by a change in another. Watch for students who call a form equal because it uses the same digits.

video_script.why: The child decides which forms are equal to a given expression by reading terms with signs, without working out the values.
video_script.substitution: Read the terms of the given expression, open any bracket, and match each form term by term.
video_script.anchor: Two given expressions, each with four forms to test
video_script.payoff_line: In set one, the first and fourth are equal, and in set two, only the fourth.

final_answer.value: (a) (i) and (iv) are equal; (ii) and (iii) are not (b) only (iv) is equal
final_answer.spoken: in set one, the first and fourth are equal, and in set two, only the fourth

never_show: the value of any form before the check step
maths_rules: (iv) −37 + 83 − 12 has the same terms in a new order, equal
(i) 84 − 38 − 12: 84 is one more and 38 is one more taken away, equal
(iii) 83 − 38 − 13 takes one extra away twice, not equal
values: 34, 34, 35, 32, 34 for the first set; 1797 for the given expression and (iv)
video_script.design: Each given expression is split into signed term cards. Each form is split the same way and matched card by card, and the cards that do not match are marked.

beats.on_screen: (a) terms: 83, −37, −12; (iv) −37 + 83 − 12 has the terms −37, 83, −12: the same, in a new order

marks.s11: the given expression is split into three cards

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, the first set, where the terms are eighty three, minus thirty seven and minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The fourth form has minus thirty seven, eighty three and minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>These are the same terms in a new order, so the fourth form is equal.

beats.on_screen: (i) 84 − 38 − 12: 84 is 83 + 1, and 38 is 37 + 1, so the + 1 and the extra − 1 cancel

marks.s21: 84 is marked as one more than 83
marks.s22: 38 is marked as one more than 37
marks.s23: the two ones cancel and the first form is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, the first form.
Eighty four is one more than eighty three.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>Thirty eight is one more than thirty seven, so one more is taken away.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>The one more added and the one more taken away cancel, so the first form is equal.

beats.on_screen: (ii) 84 − (37 + 12) = 84 − 37 − 12 starts one more, nothing cancels; (iii) 83 − 38 − 13 takes one extra away twice, two more taken away

marks.s31: the bracket of the second form opens and the signs flip
marks.s32: the 84 is marked as one more with nothing to cancel it
marks.s33: the 38 and the 13 are marked as one extra each
marks.s34: the second and third forms are crossed out

beats.colours: the crossed out forms in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, the second and third forms.
Opening the bracket in the second form gives eighty four minus thirty seven minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>It starts with eighty four, one more than eighty three, and nothing cancels.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>The third form takes one extra away from thirty seven and one extra away from twelve.
<bookmark mark='s34'/>Two more are taken away, so it is not equal.

beats.on_screen: (b) terms: 93, 37 × 44, 76; (iv) has the same three terms; (i) 93 × 44, (ii) 37 × 76 and (iii) a product of two sums change them

marks.s41: the given expression is split into three cards
marks.s42: the fourth form matches all three cards and is ticked
marks.s43: the other three forms are crossed out with their changed parts marked
marks.s44: the product of the second form is marked as changed

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, the second set.
The terms are ninety three, thirty seven times forty four, and seventy six.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>The fourth form has the same three terms in a new order, so it is equal.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>The first form changes the product to ninety three times forty four.
<bookmark mark='s44'/>The second form changes the product to thirty seven times seventy six.
The third form multiplies two sums together. These three are not equal.

marks.s51: the values of the first set are written beside each form
marks.s53: the small number check is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check the first set with values.
The given expression is thirty four, and so are the first and fourth forms.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>The second form is thirty five, and the third form is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='s53'/>For the second set, try small numbers.
<bookmark mark='s54'/>Two plus three times four plus five is nineteen.
Three times four plus two plus five is nineteen too, so moving terms keeps the total.
